salarySummary: Under the Aircraft Cabin Crew Award, a full-time air hostess (cabin crew member) earns a minimum hourly rate of $28.88, which for a 38-hour week gives an annual salary of approximately $57,066 before tax, plus super and flying allowances.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for an air hostess under the award?
faqs.a: The Aircraft Cabin Crew Award sets a minimum hourly rate of $28.88 for a full-time cabin crew member. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $36.10 per hour, plus a flying allowance of $18.40 per flying hour.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for air hostesses?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). For a full-time air hostess earning $57,066 annual salary, the employer contributes about $6,848 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

faqs.q: Does the air hostess salary include flying allowances?
faqs.a: No. The minimum rate does not include the flying allowance. The award requires an additional $18.40 per flying hour (scheduled block hours), so actual take-home can be significantly higher.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Air Hostess Salary

When you search for an "air hostess salary" in Australia, the most authoritative source is the **Aircraft Cabin Crew Award 2020** from the Fair Work Ombudsman. This award covers cabin crew members, including those commonly called air hostesses or flight attendants. It sets minimum pay rates, allowances, and conditions.

### Minimum Hourly and Weekly Rates

Under the award, a full-time cabin crew member must be paid at least **$28.88 per hour** or **$1,097.40 per week**. These rates apply from 1 July 2026. Full-time employment is defined as rostered hours between 1,716 and 1,872 per year, but the hourly rate is based on a 38-hour week for calculation purposes.

In addition to the base rate, employees receive a **flying allowance of $18.40 per hour** for scheduled block hours. This means an air hostess flying 80 hours per month could earn an extra $1,472 in allowances alone.

### Casual Loading and Pay

Casual cabin crew members are entitled to a **25% loading** on the minimum hourly rate. This is instead of paid leave and other entitlements. The casual rate is $36.10 per hour ($28.88 × 1.25). Casuals also receive the flying allowance on top, and a minimum payment of 4 hours per engagement.

### Converting Hourly to Annual Salary

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time air hostess on the minimum rate, assuming 38 hours per week:

$28.88 × 38 × 52 = **$57,066 per year**

If you include the flying allowance for, say, 80 flying hours per month (about 18.5 hours per week), the annual gross could be:

Base: $57,066 + Flying allowance: $18.40 × 18.5 × 52 = $17,707 ≈ **$74,773 total**

Use our [the timesheet](/) to enter your hourly rate and see the annual equivalent. You can also check [pay guides](/blog) for award-specific details.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many airlines pay fortnightly. Multiply your weekly rate by 2. For the minimum weekly rate of $1,097.40, a fortnightly gross is $2,194.80 before tax and allowances.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee at **12%** of ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026). This is on top of your salary, not deducted from it. For a $57,066 salary, the super contribution is about $6,848 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

### Tax on Air Hostess Salary

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Plus Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low incomes). For a $57,066 salary, tax would be approximately $7,717 plus Medicare $1,141, leaving about $48,208 after tax. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise estimate.

### Comparison with National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $33.05 casual. The air hostess award rate of $28.88 is higher, reflecting the specialised nature of the role. Casual air hostesses earn $36.10, well above the national casual minimum.

### Enterprise Agreements and Part-Time Work

Many airlines have enterprise agreements that provide pay above the award. Always check your specific employment contract. The award is the legal minimum. Part-time employees receive pro-rata entitlements and overtime for hours beyond their agreed roster.

### Summary

An air hostess salary under the Aircraft Cabin Crew Award starts at $28.88 per hour for full-time employees, plus a flying allowance. Casual workers get a 25% loading. Superannuation is paid on top at 12%. Use our calculator to estimate your annual pay based on your actual hours and allowances. Remember that the award is the minimum; many employers pay more through enterprise agreements.
